title: The Compass of Vilna
premise: In 1938 Vilna, Casper Galloway has spent three years as a mapmaker's apprentice concealing her identity and the forbidden atlas her murdered master died completing—a document that charts the hidden homes, smuggling routes, and false papers of the city's persecuted communities. When a census taker's probing question exposes her, Casper must finish the atlas's final pages and smuggle it past three checkpoints to a ship sailing on the morning tide, aided by Tomas, a border guard torn between duty and love for her. At the final checkpoint Tomas must choose between his uniform and his heart, letting her pass at the cost of his own freedom. The atlas reaches London and is published under both their names, but Casper returns to occupied Vilna to guide others out—choosing inheritance of her master's purpose over safety.
about_author: Astrid Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records in Baltic state collections. She writes historical fiction about the people history reduced to marginalia.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Casper, in close third person, works alone in the dead master's studio, inking coastlines she cannot sign with her own name. A knock at the door—the annual census taker—asks which family she belongs to. She gives the rehearsed answer, but his eyes linger on the atlas pages drying behind her. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Master Died For
chapters.summary: Flashback through Casper's POV: three years earlier, Master Levin burning his own maps as soldiers arrive, pressing the unfinished atlas into her hands and telling her silences keep people safe. Present-day Casper realizes the atlas is one chapter from complete. Beat: grief transmuted into obligation.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: The census taker returns unannounced, asking why a 'Galloway' speaks Yiddish in her sleep. Casper deflects, but he leaves a summons card: verification hearing in six days. Her neighbor Rivke warns that verified means registered, and registered means listed. Beat: invisibility collapses.

chapters.title: The Cartography of Escape
chapters.summary: Casper studies the atlas's smugglers' routes and finds the final missing section: the harbor district, redrawn after last spring's checkpoint changes. She needs someone who knows the new guard rotations. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Guard at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Tomas Vaitkus, POV shift, checks papers at the fish market and notices a young mapmaker watching him count soldiers. He lets a fishwife's expired permit slide—an old weakness. Their eyes meet; he recognizes her from the university lecture hall, before everything changed. Beat: recognition and unease.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Uniforms
chapters.summary: Casper approaches Tomas under pretense of commissioning a survey map, probing what he knows about the harbor checkpoints. He suspects her game but is drawn to her steadiness. She leaves without an answer—and without realizing he copied the address off her permit. Beat: dangerous mutual curiosity.

chapters.title: Rivke's Basement Press
chapters.summary: Rivke reveals an underground network printing false papers and asks whether the atlas could guide their couriers. Casper refuses to risk the original but agrees to copy the route plates. Inking duplicates by lamplight, she understands she has already chosen a side. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Casper faces the verification board, reciting her fabricated lineage while the census taker watches like a hawk. A forged baptismal record from Rivke's press saves her—for now—but the clerk notes discrepancies. Walking out, she passes a line of families being turned away. Beat: survival laced with shame.

chapters.title: Rain on the Rooftops
chapters.summary: Tomas finds Casper sketching rooftops near the river and, instead of arresting her, walks with her, talking about the Lithuania they were promised as students. She tests him with a half-truth about the atlas; he doesn't report her. Beat: love kindling against instinct.

chapters.title: What Duty Weighs
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV: his brother, a true believer, warns him he's being watched for leniency. Ordered to compile lists of suspicious residents, Tomas omits the mapmaker's name and hates himself for how easily the pen lies. Beat: complicity and self-division.

chapters.title: The Missing Plate
chapters.summary: Casper discovers the atlas's harbor plate stolen from the studio—someone searched while she was at the hearing. The census taker? Or Rivke's network covering itself? With four days until the tide, she must redraw it from memory. Beat: betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: Confessions by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Casper tells Tomas everything: the master's murder, the atlas, the ship. Instead of turning her in, he memorizes the new checkpoint schedule and offers to walk her through the first gate himself. They admit what they are to each other without naming it. Beat: trust as surrender.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Paper Gate
chapters.summary: Disguised as a commercial courier, Casper carries the atlas in a map tube stamped with official seals Tomas provided. The clerk scrutinizes her forged transit pass; a dropped glove nearly betrays her shaking hands. She passes. Beat: terror mastered, barely.

chapters.title: The Brother's Shadow
chapters.summary: Tomas's brother reports the missing seal stamps. Interrogated, Tomas claims burglary, buying Casper hours but painting a target on them both. He burns his own letters home. Beat: the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Rivke's Choice
chapters.summary: Rivke confesses she took the plate—not to betray Casper but because the network needed it and couldn't wait for her caution. She returns it, along with a place on the ship for two. Casper must decide whether to flee or stay and finish the last chapter. Beat: forgiveness and fracture.

chapters.title: The Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Through the night, Casper inks the harbor section from memory—every safe house, every blind alley, every name the master trusted her to carry. At dawn she signs it: his name, then hers, then Tomas's. Beat: inheritance claimed.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The River Gate
chapters.summary: Tomas walks Casper through the river checkpoint wearing his own escort authority, knowing it will be logged against him. His commanding officer appears; Tomas produces falsified orders he prepared days ago. They pass, but the officer's stare follows them. Beat: love spending its collateral.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bakery
chapters.summary: The census taker, tipped by the brother, waits at the pre-arranged rendezvous. Rivke is seized; Casper escapes through the bakery's cellar into the catacombs beneath the old city, guided by her own cartography. Beat: the map becomes the territory.

chapters.title: Underground
chapters.summary: Lost in the tunnels, Casper navigates by compass and memory toward the harbor, finding the smugglers' marks the master taught her to read. Above, sirens. She emerges at dawn behind the fish market, atlas intact, hands bleeding. Beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: The final gate is locked down; the ship sails in two hours. Tomas arrives in full uniform, orders in hand, and demands the gate opened for an 'evidence transfer.' The officer from the river checkpoint challenges him. Guns come level. Beat: the cliff's edge.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Tomas names himself a traitor rather than let them search the tube, buying Casper the gangway with his arrest. From the deck she watches him stand straight as they take him, neither looking away. The atlas goes into the diplomatic pouch. Beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: The Compass True North
chapters.summary: Epilogue, 1946: the atlas published in London saves hundreds of routes used by escape networks. Casper, back in Vilna working the underground, receives a letter in Tomas's hand—he survived the camps. The final page shows a hand-drawn compass whose needle points not north, but home. Beat: resolution, return, hope.
